items.stem: The explosion of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor in February 1898 was used to justify war with Spain. Which of the following best evaluates how this event functioned within a broader causal framework for the Spanish-American War?
items.stemEs: La explosión del USS Maine en el Puerto de La Habana en febrero de 1898 se usó para justificar la guerra con España. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor cómo este evento funcionó dentro de un marco causal más amplio para la Guerra Hispano-Americana?

choices.text: The Maine explosion was the fundamental underlying cause of the Spanish-American War; without the explosion and the emotional public reaction it generated, there would have been no political will or congressional support for war.
choices.textEs: La explosión del Maine fue la causa subyacente fundamental de la Guerra Hispano-Americana, y sin ella no habría habido guerra.

choices.text: The Maine explosion was definitively proven to have been caused by Spanish naval sabotage, which gave the McKinley administration an unambiguous legal and moral justification for declaring war on Spain.
choices.textEs: Se demostró que la explosión del Maine fue causada por España, lo que le dio a Estados Unidos una clara justificación legal para declarar la guerra.

choices.text: The Maine explosion was a precipitating event providing immediate political justification for a war that pre-existing conditions — Cuban unrest, yellow journalism, economic interests, and imperial ambitions — had already made likely.
choices.textEs: La explosión del Maine fue un evento precipitante que proporcionó justificación política inmediata para una guerra que las condiciones preexistentes — el malestar cubano, el periodismo amarillista, los intereses económicos y las ambiciones imperiales — ya habían hecho probable.

choices.text: The Maine explosion had no significant political impact because the McKinley administration had already made a firm and irreversible internal decision to go to war with Spain before the explosion occurred in Havana Harbor.
choices.textEs: La explosión del Maine no tuvo un impacto político significativo porque la administración McKinley ya había decidido ir a la guerra con España antes de que ocurriera la explosión.

items.explanation: The USS Maine explosion was a precipitating event — it provided the immediate emotional trigger and political justification for war — but it was not the underlying cause. The underlying causes had been building for years: Cuban rebellion against Spanish rule, Spanish atrocities reported by yellow journalists, U.S. economic interests in Cuba (sugar), humanitarian concern for Cuba, and imperial ambitions. The Maine gave interventionists the public outrage they needed to overcome remaining hesitation. Without the pre-existing conditions, the Maine alone would not have caused war; without the Maine, war might have come by another route. Option A confuses precipitating with underlying cause; Option B is historically inaccurate; Option D understates the Maine's political significance.
items.explanationEs: La explosión del USS Maine fue un evento precipitante — proporcionó el detonante emocional inmediato y la justificación política para la guerra — pero no fue la causa subyacente. Las causas subyacentes se habían estado acumulando durante años: la rebelión cubana contra el dominio español, las atrocidades españolas reportadas por periodistas amarillistas, los intereses económicos de EE. UU. en Cuba (azúcar) y las ambiciones imperiales. La opción A confunde la causa precipitante con la subyacente; la B es históricamente inexacta; la D subestima la importancia política del Maine.

items.explanation: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) had always asserted a U.S. sphere of influence in the Western Hemisphere by warning European powers against further colonization. The Roosevelt Corollary did not abandon this framework but transformed it: where Monroe had been primarily defensive (keeping Europe out), Roosevelt made it offensive (the U.S. would act as a 'hemispheric policeman'). The Corollary was an evolution because it built on the same foundational claim — U.S. dominance in the hemisphere — while dramatically expanding the scope of what the U.S. claimed the right to do. This represents policy evolution, not revolution. Options A and D identify specific but incomplete aspects; Option C mischaracterizes the Monroe Doctrine.
items.explanationEs: La Doctrina Monroe (1823) siempre había afirmado una esfera de influencia de EE. UU. en el Hemisferio Occidental al advertir a las potencias europeas contra una mayor colonización. El Corolario Roosevelt no abandonó este marco sino que lo transformó: donde Monroe había sido principalmente defensivo, Roosevelt lo hizo ofensivo (EE. UU. actuaría como 'policía hemisférico'). La opción A identifica un aspecto específico pero incompleto; la C caracteriza incorrectamente la Doctrina Monroe; la D también es incompleta.

items.stem: The outcomes of the Spanish-American War — control of Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines — dramatically transformed the United States' strategic position. Which of the following best assesses whether these gains justified the costs of the war and its aftermath?
items.stemEs: Los resultados de la Guerra Hispano-Americana — control de Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam y las Filipinas — transformaron dramáticamente la posición estratégica de Estados Unidos. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor si estas ganancias justificaron los costos de la guerra y sus consecuencias?

choices.text: The strategic gains fully justified all costs because the United States became a global power with negligible long-term negative consequences.
choices.textEs: Las ganancias estratégicas justificaron plenamente todos los costos porque Estados Unidos se convirtió en una potencia global con consecuencias negativas a largo plazo insignificantes.

choices.text: The costs clearly outweighed the gains because the Philippine-American War proved that colonial administration was never worth the military and financial burden.
choices.textEs: Los costos claramente superaron las ganancias porque la Guerra Filipino-Americana demostró que la administración colonial nunca valió la carga militar y financiera.

choices.text: The question of whether the gains justified the costs is unanswerable because historical outcomes cannot be evaluated in terms of trade-offs.
choices.textEs: La pregunta de si las ganancias justificaron los costos no tiene respuesta porque los resultados históricos no pueden evaluarse en términos de compensaciones.

choices.text: The gains produced real strategic and commercial benefits, but the costs — including the brutal Philippine-American War, unresolved questions about colonial peoples' constitutional status
choices.textEs: Las ganancias produjeron beneficios estratégicos y comerciales reales, pero los costos — incluyendo la brutal Guerra Filipino-Americana, las preguntas no resueltas sobre el estatus constitucional de los pueblos coloniales y el sentimiento anti-americano a largo plazo — requieren una evaluación equilibrada que resista la simple vindicación.

items.explanation: This is a genuine historical cost-benefit question with no simple answer, and the most defensible response acknowledges the complexity. Strategic gains were real: the U.S. became a Pacific power, acquired vital naval bases, demonstrated global military capability, and expanded commercial reach. But costs were also real: the Philippine-American War cost far more in lives and money than anticipated, generated lasting anti-American sentiment in Asia, raised unresolved constitutional questions about the status of colonial peoples, and created security commitments that would complicate future policy. A sophisticated assessment must weigh these competing considerations. Options A and B are simplistic verdicts; Option C avoids the evaluative question.
items.explanationEs: Esta es una genuina pregunta histórica de costo-beneficio sin una respuesta simple, y la respuesta más defendible reconoce la complejidad. Las ganancias estratégicas fueron reales: EE. UU. se convirtió en potencia del Pacífico, adquirió bases navales vitales y expandió el alcance comercial. Pero los costos también fueron reales: la Guerra Filipino-Americana costó mucho más en vidas y dinero de lo anticipado, generó sentimiento anti-americano duradero en Asia y planteó preguntas constitucionales no resueltas. Las opciones A y B son veredictos simplistas; la C evita la pregunta evaluativa.

items.stem: Between 1898 and 1914, the United States intervened militarily in Cuba, Nicaragua, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic under the Roosevelt Corollary. Which of the following best explains the pattern that emerges from these interventions?
items.stemEs: Entre 1898 y 1914, Estados Unidos intervino militarmente en Cuba, Nicaragua, Haití y la República Dominicana bajo el Corolario Roosevelt. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor el patrón que emerge de estas intervenciones?

choices.text: U.S. interventions consistently aligned with American strategic and economic interests — particularly protecting the Panama Canal approaches and preventing European creditor nations from gaining Caribbean footholds
choices.textEs: Las intervenciones de EE. UU. se alinearon consistentemente con los intereses estratégicos y económicos americanos — particularmente proteger los accesos al Canal de Panamá e impedir que las naciones acreedoras europeas ganaran puntos de apoyo en el Caribe — revelando el Corolario como un instrumento de hegemonía de EE. UU. en lugar de pacificación desinteresada.

choices.text: U.S. interventions consistently failed to achieve their stated goals, producing greater instability than existed before American forces arrived.
choices.textEs: Las intervenciones de EE. UU. consistentemente no lograron sus objetivos declarados, produciendo mayor inestabilidad de la que existía antes de la llegada de las fuerzas americanas.

choices.text: The interventions were entirely humanitarian in motivation, driven by genuine concern for the welfare of Caribbean populations rather than U.S. strategic interests.
choices.textEs: Las intervenciones fueron enteramente humanitarias en motivación, impulsadas por una preocupación genuina por el bienestar de las poblaciones caribeñas en lugar de los intereses estratégicos de EE. UU.

choices.text: No consistent pattern emerges from these interventions because each case was unique and driven by entirely different factors.
choices.textEs: No surge un patrón consistente de estas intervenciones porque cada caso fue único e impulsado por factores completamente diferentes.

items.explanation: The pattern across these interventions reveals that the stated justification (maintaining order, protecting debt repayment) consistently aligned with U.S. strategic and economic interests — specifically, protecting the approaches to the Panama Canal and preventing European creditor nations from establishing footholds in the Caribbean. The trigger for intervention was typically financial instability or political disorder, but the underlying logic was always about maintaining U.S. hegemony in the Caribbean basin. This demonstrates that the Roosevelt Corollary functioned as an ideological framework for enforcing U.S. dominance rather than a genuinely impartial peacekeeping mandate. Options B and C are empirically inaccurate; Option D ignores the consistent pattern.
items.explanationEs: El patrón a través de estas intervenciones revela que la justificación declarada (mantener el orden, proteger el pago de deudas) coincidía consistentemente con los intereses estratégicos y económicos de EE. UU. — específicamente, proteger los accesos al Canal de Panamá e impedir que las naciones acreedoras europeas establecieran puntos de apoyo en el Caribe. Las opciones B y C son empíricamente inexactas; la D ignora el patrón consistente.

items.stem: The Insular Cases (1901) established that the Constitution did not fully apply to U.S. territories. Which of the following best evaluates how these Supreme Court decisions reflected broader tensions in American imperialism?
items.stemEs: Los Casos Insulares (1901) establecieron que la Constitución no se aplicaba completamente a los territorios de EE. UU. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor cómo estas decisiones de la Corte Suprema reflejaron tensiones más amplias en el imperialismo americano?

choices.text: The Insular Cases resolved all constitutional tensions by extending full constitutional rights to all U.S. territorial residents.
choices.textEs: Los Casos Insulares resolvieron todas las tensiones constitucionales al extender plenos derechos constitucionales a todos los residentes de los territorios de EE. UU.

choices.text: The Insular Cases demonstrated the democratic character of American imperialism by establishing that colonial peoples would eventually receive full constitutional rights.
choices.textEs: Los Casos Insulares demostraron el carácter democrático del imperialismo americano al establecer que los pueblos coloniales eventualmente recibirían plenos derechos constitucionales.

choices.text: The Insular Cases legally codified the core contradiction of American imperialism by creating a colonial legal category that allowed the U.S.
choices.textEs: Los Casos Insulares codificaron legalmente la contradicción central del imperialismo americano al crear una categoría legal colonial que permitió a EE. UU. gobernar territorios y pueblos sin extender las plenas protecciones constitucionales, reflejando la jerarquía racial incorporada en la política imperial.

choices.text: The Insular Cases had no racial dimension and were purely technical decisions about the limits of federal jurisdiction.
choices.textEs: Los Casos Insulares no tenían dimensión racial y fueron decisiones puramente técnicas sobre los límites de la jurisdicción federal.

items.explanation: The Insular Cases formalized the constitutional contradiction at the heart of American imperialism: the U.S. wanted the economic and strategic benefits of colonial possession without the political obligation to extend full constitutional rights to colonial subjects. The rulings created a legal category of 'unincorporated territories' — essentially a colonial category without a path to statehood — that allowed the U.S. to administer colonial peoples without treating them as future citizens. This reflected and legally codified the racial hierarchy embedded in American imperialism. Option A mischaracterizes the decisions; Option B overstates their democratic character; Option D ignores the explicit racial dimension the Justices themselves invoked.
items.explanationEs: Los Casos Insulares formalizaron la contradicción constitucional en el corazón del imperialismo americano: EE. UU. quería los beneficios económicos y estratégicos de la posesión colonial sin la obligación política de extender los plenos derechos constitucionales a los súbditos coloniales. Los fallos crearon una categoría legal de 'territorios no incorporados' — esencialmente una categoría colonial sin vía hacia la estadidad — que permitió a EE. UU. administrar pueblos coloniales sin tratarlos como futuros ciudadanos. La opción A caracteriza incorrectamente las decisiones; la B exagera su carácter democrático; la D ignora la dimensión racial explícita.

items.stem: Based on the map, what was a primary strategic and economic benefit of the Panama Canal for the United States?

choices.text: It significantly shortened shipping routes between the Atlantic and Pacific coasts
It opened direct U.S. trade with Africa for the first time
It allowed the United States to claim South American territory
It eliminated the need for a U.S. Navy in the Atlantic Ocean

items.explanation: The canal let ships move between the Atlantic and Pacific without rounding South America, cutting thousands of miles from the voyage and letting the Navy shift fleets between oceans quickly. Choice B is wrong because the canal linked the Americas, not the United States and Africa. Choice D is wrong because a shorter route made the Atlantic fleet more useful, not unnecessary. Speed of naval movement was the strategic argument that made the canal a national priority.
items.explanationEs: La política de Theodore Roosevelt en Panamá combinó el apoyo a la independencia panameña de Colombia (1903), el Tratado Hay-Bunau-Varilla que otorgó a EE. UU. derechos sobre el canal y la afirmación del «gran garrote» del poder hemisférico estadounidense. El canal se abrió al tráfico el 15 de agosto de 1914. (Fuente: history.state.gov — Construcción del Canal de Panamá.)

items.stem: Which conclusion about the Harlem Renaissance is best supported by its emergence in New York City during the 1920s?

choices.text: African American cultural expression flourished most in regions where state-level racial segregation laws were entirely absent.
The Great Migration created concentrated African American communities in Northern cities that became centers of cultural and intellectual achievement.
African American artists deliberately rejected Southern cultural and musical traditions in favor of European artistic forms.
The economic prosperity of the 1920s provided African Americans equal access to economic opportunity for the first time since Reconstruction.

items.explanation: The Great Migration (1910–1970) relocated hundreds of thousands of African Americans to Northern cities. Harlem became a destination for Black intellectuals, artists, and writers, and its concentrated community enabled the cultural flowering known as the Harlem Renaissance.

items.stem:
Extended Response: U.S. Foreign Policy and the Limits of Power, 1898–1920

Using your knowledge of U.S. history, write an extended essay that evaluates the following question: How did the acquisition of overseas territories between 1898 and 1920 change the United States' relationship with the rest of the world, and to what extent did those changes create new problems that the United States struggled to manage?

Your essay must draw on at least three specific examples, construct a clear argument about the costs and consequences of territorial expansion, connect your analysis to the principles stated in the Monroe Doctrine and the Fourteen Points, and explain how the tensions created by empire-building shaped U.S. foreign policy decisions during this period. Your response should acknowledge the perspective of people in the acquired territories — in the Philippines, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Cuba, or Panama — and evaluate how those perspectives challenge or complicate traditional narratives of American expansion.
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida: La Política Exterior de EE. UU. y los Límites del Poder, 1898–1920

Usando su conocimiento de la historia de EE. UU., escriba un ensayo extendido que evalúe la siguiente pregunta: ¿Cómo cambió la adquisición de territorios de ultramar entre 1898 y 1920 la relación de los Estados Unidos con el resto del mundo, y en qué medida crearon esos cambios nuevos problemas que los Estados Unidos tuvo dificultades para manejar?

Su ensayo debe apoyarse en al menos tres ejemplos específicos, construir un argumento claro sobre los costos y consecuencias de la expansión territorial, conectar su análisis con los principios establecidos en la Doctrina Monroe y los Catorce Puntos, y explicar cómo las tensiones creadas por la construcción del imperio moldearon las decisiones de política exterior de EE. UU. durante este período. Su respuesta debe reconocer la perspectiva de las personas en los territorios adquiridos — en las Filipinas, Hawái, Puerto Rico, Cuba o Panamá — y evaluar cómo esas perspectivas desafían o complican las narrativas tradicionales de la expansión americana.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response makes a complex, defensible claim — such as: 'The acquisition of overseas territories between 1898 and 1920 transformed the United States from a continental into a global power, but this transformation generated persistent contradictions — between democratic ideals and imperial practice, between strategic ambition and administrative capability, and between American promises and territorial realities — that left the U.S. managing an empire it was ideologically unprepared to own.' At least three specific examples: (1) Philippines — Philippine-American War (1899–1902) cost the U.S. approximately $400 million and 4,234 U.S. deaths, with Filipino casualties estimated in the hundreds of thousands; Emilio Aguinaldo's resistance revealed that Filipinos did not regard U.S. rule as liberation; Insular Cases (1901) created a legal second-class status for territorial residents. (2) Cuba — Platt Amendment (1901) transformed the promised independence (Teller) into a protectorate; U.S. military occupation lasted until 1902, with re-interventions in 1906 and 1912; this planted the seeds of anti-American nationalism that would eventually produce the Cuban Revolution (1959). (3) Panama — U.S. engineering of independence (1903) and the 10-mile Canal Zone created lasting resentment in Panama (which eventually led to the Torrijos-Carter Treaties of 1977). Connection to Monroe Doctrine: Monroe's defensive posture became Roosevelt's 'police power' claim — the acquired territories required active administration and protection, generating the very interventionist pattern Monroe had tried to avoid. Connection to Fourteen Points: Wilson's call for self-determination and open covenants directly contradicted the reality of U.S. territorial governance; colonial peoples noted the hypocrisy. Territory-holder perspectives: Filipino nationalists under Aguinaldo argued the U.S. had betrayed its own Declaration of Independence; Puerto Ricans received Jones Act citizenship (1917) without full representation; Native Hawaiians lost their queen and sovereignty in 1893; Panamanians gained nominal independence but lost sovereignty over the Canal Zone.

SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Complex, defensible claim about contradictions created by empire. Three or more specific examples with accurate evidence that includes perspectives of people in acquired territories. Explicit connection to Monroe Doctrine and Fourteen Points showing how imperial practice contradicted stated principles. Analysis of how these tensions shaped later foreign policy decisions (Roosevelt Corollary as formalization of problems, WWI debate as a product of expanded global entanglement). Well-organized, with clear argument progression.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim about costs/consequences. Two or more specific examples. Some inclusion of territorial perspectives. Connections to Monroe Doctrine or Fourteen Points present. Argument is coherent if not fully nuanced.
2 - Developing: Claim present but vague. One or two examples, limited territorial perspectives. Limited connection to Monroe Doctrine or Fourteen Points. More descriptive than analytical.
1 - Beginning: Little or no claim. Vague examples. No territorial perspectives. No connections to other standards or eras.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Philippine-American War (1899–1902) — costs, Aguinaldo, Insular Cases; Cuba — Teller Amendment promise, Platt Amendment betrayal, protectorate interventions (1906, 1912); Panama — 1903 revolution, Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty, Canal Zone; Hawaii — 1893 overthrow, Organic Act (1900); Insular Cases (1901); Jones Act Puerto Rico (1917); Anti-Imperialist League; Monroe Doctrine non-interventionism vs. Roosevelt Corollary police power; Wilson's Fourteen Points self-determination vs. colonial reality.
SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: The question requires connecting three standards (US.21, US.22, US.23) and linking to US.19 (causes) and US.27 (Fourteen Points/post-war); a strong response shows how imperial acquisitions created the entanglements and resentments that constrained later U.S. foreign policy and complicated Wilson's peace vision; the perspective-taking requirement elevates this to genuine cross-standard synthesis.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Afirmación compleja y defendible sobre las contradicciones creadas por el imperio. Tres o más ejemplos específicos con evidencia precisa que incluye perspectivas de personas en territorios adquiridos. Conexión explícita con la Doctrina Monroe y los Catorce Puntos. Análisis de cómo estas tensiones moldearon las decisiones de política exterior posteriores. Bien organizado.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara sobre costos/consecuencias. Dos o más ejemplos específicos. Alguna inclusión de perspectivas territoriales. Conexiones con la Doctrina Monroe o los Catorce Puntos presentes.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación presente pero vaga. Uno o dos ejemplos, perspectivas territoriales limitadas. Conexión limitada con la Doctrina Monroe o los Catorce Puntos.
1 - Inicial: Poca o ninguna afirmación. Ejemplos vagos. Sin perspectivas territoriales.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera de tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Guerra Filipino-Americana (1899–1902) — costos, Aguinaldo, Casos Insulares; Cuba — Enmienda Teller, Enmienda Platt, intervenciones como protectorado; Panamá — revolución de 1903, Tratado Hay-Bunau-Varilla, Zona del Canal; Hawái — derrocamiento de 1893, Ley Orgánica (1900); Jones Act Puerto Rico (1917); Liga Antiimperialista; Doctrina Monroe vs. Corolario Roosevelt; Catorce Puntos de Wilson vs. realidad colonial.
EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: La pregunta requiere conectar tres estándares (US.21, US.22, US.23) y vincular con US.19 y US.27; una respuesta sólida muestra cómo las adquisiciones imperiales crearon los compromisos y resentimientos que limitaron la política exterior posterior de EE. UU.
